text: CHAPTER 8
speaker: Narrator

text: Four Working
speaker: Narrator
note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

text: The first shifted street they found together was almost polite about it.
speaker: Narrator

text: It began as an ordinary alley behind a row of dye-works in the lower western district. The morning air there tasted of copper, vinegar, and wet wool. Strips of dyed cloth hung from upper windows, dripping red and indigo onto the packed earth below. Workers moved between vats with their arms stained to the elbow, shouting measurements at one another over the hiss of boiling water.
speaker: Narrator

text: By the time Zik and the others reached the middle of the alley, the noise had thinned.
speaker: Narrator

text: The walls had grown older.
speaker: Narrator

text: The bricks darkened from sun-baked brown to a nearly black clay that held a faint sheen beneath the grime. The air cooled against Zik's face, carrying the mineral smell of sealed stone and standing water. Behind them, a dye-worker cursed as someone spilled a vat.
speaker: Narrator

text: The voice sounded much farther away than it should have.
speaker: Narrator

text: Where the alley ought to have ended against the back of a warehouse, it simply continued—a narrow descending passage that none of the city maps recorded and none of the locals would admit existed when asked.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag stopped at the change in the masonry and tested the ground with the butt of his spear.
speaker: Narrator

text: This wasn't here yesterday.
speaker: Balag

text: It wasn't here when we turned the corner,
speaker: Enhedu

text: Enhedu said.
speaker: Narrator
note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

text: She was already examining the join where new brick met old. The seam did not look built. It looked grown. One wall belonged to a warehouse raised within living memory. The other had been worn smooth by hands that had not touched it in centuries.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun had her stylus out before the rest of them finished speaking.
speaker: Narrator

text: She pressed a damp clay tablet against her forearm and began copying the seam with the focused intensity of someone who had waited years for the city to make a mistake she could catch in writing.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag glanced at the tablet.
speaker: Narrator

text: You planning to arrest it?
speaker: Balag

text: I'm documenting it.
speaker: Ninsun

text: So we can arrest it later.
speaker: Balag

text: So when the alley disappears, one of us possesses proof it existed.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Enhedu leaned closer to the bricks.
speaker: Narrator

text: Clay changes.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Not without leaving a mark.
speaker: Ninsun

text: This city seems fond of exceptions.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Ninsun did not look up.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then I'll document the exception.
speaker: Ninsun

text: Zik stood back and watched the three of them settle into the work without discussion.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag checked structure.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu checked value.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ninsun checked history.
speaker: Narrator

text: The division of labor had formed in less than a day and no one had needed to declare it.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik checked the exits.
speaker: Narrator

text: Behind them, the alley remained open. A blue length of cloth stirred above the entrance. Beyond it, people moved across the ordinary street without looking in. One man stopped near the mouth of the alley, adjusted a jar against his hip, and continued walking as if four people had not just vanished into a passage where no passage belonged.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik took a length of chalk from his pouch and drew a short line across the bricks at shoulder height.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu watched him.
speaker: Narrator

text: So we know whether the wall moves?
speaker: Enhedu

text: So we know whether we do.
speaker: Zik

text: Balag gave the dark passage another look.
speaker: Narrator

text: That sentence made things worse.
speaker: Balag

text: It wasn't meant to help.
speaker: Zik

text: They moved in the order that was already becoming habit: Balag first, Enhedu second, Ninsun third, Zik last.
speaker: Narrator

text: The walls narrowed until shoulders brushed stone. The temperature dropped with every dozen steps. Somewhere ahead water dripped with the slow patience of a place that had never needed to hurry.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik counted the steps.
speaker: Narrator

text: Twelve to the first turn.
speaker: Narrator

text: Nine to the second.
speaker: Narrator

text: Then fourteen down a slope so gradual he felt it more in his knees than saw it beneath his feet.
speaker: Narrator

text: At the twenty-seventh step, the noise of the dye-works disappeared completely.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag raised a hand.
speaker: Narrator
